description:
src/methods/metadata.rs:130-156 — metadata_set takes update: Option<HashMap<Id, PatchObject>>. Id is re-exported via 'pub use jmap_types::{…}' in jmap-types but PatchObject is NOT in the lib.rs re-export list (lib.rs:30-33: AddedItem, ChangesResponse, GetResponse, MetadataChangesParams, QueryChangesResponse, QueryResponse, SessionClient, SetError, SetResponse). State is also not re-exported.

A caller that depends only on 'jmap-metadata-client' in their Cargo.toml hits this compile error:

    use jmap_metadata_client::PatchObject;  // error: no `PatchObject` in the root
    use jmap_types::PatchObject;            // error: jmap_types is not declared

…and must add jmap-types as a direct dep just to construct the update argument. Same applies to Id (referenced as Option<&[Id]> in metadata_get and as Vec<Id> in metadata_set's destroy arg) and State (referenced as &State in metadata_changes and metadata_query_changes).

This isn't a contract immutability problem — adding re-exports is backwards-compatible. But it is a docs/ergonomics gap that forces every downstream caller to read the function signatures, deduce which sibling-crate types they need, and amend Cargo.toml accordingly.

Workspace-wide observation: canonical mail-client/src/lib.rs has the same gap. So fixing this requires propagating a 'pub use jmap_types::{Id, PatchObject, State}' re-export pattern through every *-client crate. Cheap and additive.

Fix: extend lib.rs re-exports to:
    pub use jmap_types::{Id, PatchObject, State};

And document in the lib.rs preamble that these are re-exported for caller convenience.
title: PatchObject not re-exported — callers must add jmap-types dep just to call metadata_set
